GUARDRAIL: influence/goodness is NOT truth — a faith can shape the world and still be false; stated plainly. Tom Holland = 'the historian' (NOT 'secular historian' [stale] and NOT 'apologist'). voiceover: How much of the modern world is quietly downstream of Christianity? This section traces the fingerprints. How a tiny, illegal, persecuted sect became the faith of an empire. Where our deepest assumptions came from — that every human being is equal, and that the weak deserve care. The Christian roots of modern science, the end of the slave trade, and the very idea of progress. And the honest question the section refuses to dodge — does shaping the world make a faith true? It does not, and we say so plainly. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. What this section makes the case for is narrower, and harder to shrug off: that the moral world a sceptic takes for granted is more Christian than they know — reason enough to look again. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
